author: praasz
title: GPU unit tests fail with a burst of 37 gtest-parallel worker crashes right after fp16_scale_out accuracy mismatch
signature: GPU unit tests accuracy tolerance mismatch in fusion test (val_ref vs val_opt difference exceeds tolerance in fusion_test_common.hpp) followed by burst of concurrent gtest-parallel worker processes exiting with code 3|Flaky Test

failed_jobs.name: GPU unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: First test fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out/1 fails on a tiny fp16 accuracy tolerance mismatch, followed by 36 other gtest-parallel worker processes exiting with exit code 3 (crash/abort) across unrelated test suites (convolution smoke tests, fusings, etc.).

key_errors: fusion_test_common.hpp(90): error: The difference between val_ref[i] and val_opt[i] is 3.0517578125e-05, which exceeds tolerance, where val_ref[i] evaluates to -0.04473876953125, val_opt[i] evaluates to -0.044769287109375, tolerance evaluates to 9.9999997473787516e-06
root_cause: The run matches a known recurring pattern: 'GPU unit tests' job on the Windows (VS 2022, Release) post-commit pipeline begins with a tiny fp16 numeric tolerance mismatch in fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out/1 (difference ~3e-5 vs tolerance ~1e-5, a borderline fp16 rounding issue in the fused pooling+scale kernel), and is immediately followed by 36 additional gtest-parallel worker processes exiting with exit code 3 across otherwise-unrelated test cases (convolution smoke tests, fusings). Exit code 3 for unrelated, non-executing tests (RUN logged but test body never completes) is consistent with worker-process level instability (e.g., GPU driver/device contention or resource exhaustion under gtest-parallel's concurrent worker model) rather than 37 independent logic bugs. This same signature has now recurred 4 times (today's run makes it the 4th... now 5th) over the past day on this workflow, reinforcing the 'Flaky Test'/infrastructure-adjacent classification rather than a new code regression introduced by PR #39575 (an HSM-reader exception-handling change unrelated to GPU kernels).
reproduction_steps: On a Windows GPU test runner: build GPU unit tests, then run `python gtest-parallel.py ... ov_gpu_unit_tests.exe --gtest_filter=fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out/1` repeatedly to check for fp16 tolerance flakiness, and separately run the full suite concurrently via gtest-parallel to attempt to reproduce the cascading exit-code-3 crashes under worker contention. Not reliably reproducible outside the shared CI runner environment.
recommended_actions: Escalate signature 502c01bffd8f35db to the GPU plugin test owners given it has now recurred 5 times in ~24h on master post-commit Windows GPU unit tests.

Investigate whether the Windows GPU runner pool has a shared/contended GPU device causing exit code 3 bursts under gtest-parallel; check runner logs for GPU driver resets or OOM during the affected time window.

Consider loosening the fp16 tolerance in fusion_test_common.hpp for pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out or marking it as a known-flaky/soft-fail case if the ~3e-5 vs ~1e-5 delta is an expected fp16 rounding edge case on this hardware.
Add gtest-parallel worker crash diagnostics (stderr/exit reason capture) so exit-code-3 bursts can be root-caused precisely instead of inferred.
prevention_strategies: Track this signature's recurrence count centrally (already done via patterns/502c01bffd8f35db.json) and set an automatic escalation threshold (e.g., notify GPU plugin owners directly) once a pattern's count crosses a small number of occurrences in a short window, since manual Teams reports may be missed. Consider adding retry-on-crash logic in the Windows GPU unit test job for gtest-parallel worker-level exit code 3 failures distinct from genuine assertion failures.
historical_context: Identical or near-identical failure signature (502c01bffd8f35db) previously recorded 4 times on 2026-11-13T17:54:36Z, 2026-11-13T22:10:58Z, 2026-11-14T01:16:34Z, and 2026-11-14T02:50:26Z, all on the same 'GPU unit tests' job starting with the fp16_scale_out tolerance mismatch and cascading into dozens of exit-code-3 worker crashes. This run is the 5th occurrence, confirming an ongoing, unresolved flaky/infrastructure issue rather than a one-off.
